title: Risk: which product, which heading, which role
blurb: Place any piece of risk information in the right product and register heading, and match each risk action to the right role in a scenario.
question: At Brennan Mutual, a statement reads 'Nicola Graham will book an early certification slot with the payments vendor by Friday.' Under which risk register heading does it belong, and why is it not the risk owner heading?

teach.h: Two risk products, two different jobs
teach.body: Formally, the risk management approach (part of the PID) describes how risk will be managed: the procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities. The risk register (part of the project log) records the identified risks, both threats and opportunities, with their status and history. In plain English: the approach is the rulebook, the register is the list of actual risks. Practitioner matching sets ask you to place statements under register headings, so learn to hear what each statement is describing.

rows.label: Answers
values: How do we manage risk here?
Which risks do we face now?

rows.label: Who signs it off
values: Kept up to date, not approved

teach.caption: A named threat written into the approach is a classic wrong answer in the Practitioner paper.

teach.h: Register headings and how they sound
head: Heading
The statement sounds like...

An estimate of the effect: 'five weeks late, £60k'
What will be done: 'reduce by booking a slot early'
Who is responsible for managing the response

teach.caption: Register headings in the sample papers (9.5). Risk exposure for a single risk is NOT a register heading.

teach.h: Risk owner or risk action owner?
teach.body: The risk owner is the person assigned to take responsibility for responding to a risk: usually someone senior enough to manage it. The risk action owner (also called the risk actionee) is the person nominated to own an agreed action in that response, often asked by the risk owner. Exam tip: if the statement names a person doing a specific task by a date, it is the risk action owner; if it names the person accountable for the whole response, it is the risk owner.

head: Role
Typical area of focus
rows: Sets risk policy and the risk appetite
Sets risk tolerance from that appetite
Single point of accountability for the project
Risks to the user side and the supplier side
Writes the approach; runs the procedure
Spots risks in the work package; tells the PM
teach.caption: Role areas of focus are in table 9.3 of the manual. Look them up in the open book rather than memorizing every row.

teach.h: How a new risk reaches the register
Worked scenario: Brennan Mutual, Project Skyline
teach.body: In the foundations stage, Stratoshift's delivery lead Arjun Menon tells project manager Mairi Campbell that the payments vendor may not certify the new cloud connection before wave 1. Mairi registers it: description (vendor certification is outside Stratoshift's control, so it may slip, delaying wave 1); proximity (the month before wave 1); impact (about five weeks and £60,000); response (reduce: book an early slot). Steven Clarke is risk owner; Nicola Graham, who manages vendors, is risk action owner. The very low appetite for member outages came from the society's board.

rows.label: Five-point scales for probability and impact
Likely in the month before wave 1
About five weeks late and £60,000 extra
Nicola to book a slot by Friday
A payments outage happened last night

teach.note: Ask: is it a rule, a fact about one uncertain event, or something that has already happened?

teach.text: Traps: (1) the risk management approach holds the procedure and responsibilities, never the specific risks; (2) the business layer sets the risk appetite, while the project board sets risk tolerance from it; (3) a team manager reports a new risk to the project manager, not the board; (4) something that has already happened is an issue, not a risk.

items: Approach (PID) = how risk is managed; register (project log) = the specific threats and opportunities.
Headings: description (cause, event, effect), proximity, impact, response, risk owner, risk action owner.
Risk owner manages the response; risk action owner carries out an agreed action.
Business layer: appetite. Board: tolerance and approval of the approach. PM: runs the procedure.
Team managers tell the PM; project support maintains the register.

summary: You can now place risk information in the right product and under the right register heading, and tell the risk owner from the risk action owner. You can also match risk actions to the business layer, board, project manager, team manager and project support in a scenario.

A.q: Calderbrook Borough Council's Permits Online project is in the discovery and alpha stage. Project manager Hannah Okoro is updating a threat that the council tax integration may fail its first test. She notes that it is most likely to happen in the two weeks before the private beta begins in the Old Town ward. Under which risk register heading should this note be recorded?
options: Proximity
Impact
Risk response
Risk description
A.why: Proximity records how near in time a risk might occur; 'the two weeks before the private beta' is a statement of timing (9.5).

whyNot.1: Impact is an estimate of the effect (for example days late or money lost), not when the risk might occur.
whyNot.2: The risk response describes what will be done about the risk, not its timing.
whyNot.3: The risk description sets out cause, event and effect; the timing note belongs under proximity.

A.q: Tarnside College's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the detailed design stage. The risk owner for the threat that the nacelle training rig arrives late has asked the college's procurement officer to place a deposit order with the Danish manufacturer by the end of the month. Under which heading should the procurement officer's name be recorded?
options: Risk owner
Risk action owner
Risk description
Risk response category
A.why: The procurement officer has been nominated to carry out a specific agreed action in the response, so is the risk action owner (9.2, 9.5).

whyNot.0: The risk owner is the person responsible for managing the overall response, who in this case asked the officer to act.
whyNot.2: The description sets out cause, event and effect, not who carries out an action.
whyNot.3: A response category names the type of response (for example reduce), not the person doing the work.

A.q: At Fernhollow Foods, the managing director has told the project board that the company has a very low appetite for food safety and allergen risk. The Fernhollow Kitchen project is about to start its concept and recipe stage. Who should set the measurable risk tolerance for that stage?
options: The managing director, as part of the business layer
The project manager, in the risk management approach
The technical and quality manager, as project assurance
The project board, using the company's appetite
A.why: Risk tolerance is set by the project board based on the business's overall risk appetite, and stage tolerances are set by the board (9.2.1, 11.2.1).

whyNot.0: The business layer determines the risk appetite and project tolerances; stage tolerances are set by the project board.
whyNot.1: The project manager works within the tolerances the board sets and sets work package tolerances, not stage risk tolerance.
whyNot.2: Project assurance supports the board with independent checks; it does not set tolerances.

B.q: Brennan Mutual's Project Skyline is in the foundations stage. Project manager Mairi Campbell writes: 'Because the landing zone has not yet been penetration tested, a security review may find control gaps, which would delay the pilot wave by six weeks.' Where should this statement be recorded?
options: In the risk register, as the risk description
In the risk management approach, as a key risk
In the daily log, as an informal observation
In the lessons log, as a lesson about security
B.why: It is one specific uncertain event written as cause, event and effect, so it is a risk description in the risk register (9.2, 9.5).

whyNot.1: The approach describes how risk is managed and holds no specific risks.
whyNot.2: The daily log holds informal issues and notes; a formal identified risk belongs in the register.
whyNot.3: Nothing has been learned yet; this is an uncertain future event, which is a risk.

B.q: Wenmoor Community Health's single point of access project is in the design and pilot preparation stage. Josie Barker, the clinical systems manager leading a work package, finds that the referral module may not accept referrals from carers, which could delay the Eastfield pilot. What should she do?
options: Raise an exception report to the project board
Add the threat to the risk management approach
Ask the medical director to choose a response
Notify the project manager, Ellie Chandran
B.why: When executing a work package, the team manager notifies the project manager of new issues, risks or lessons; the PM then captures and assesses it (17.4.2, 16.4.5).

whyNot.0: Team managers report to the project manager, and a new risk is not by itself a forecast breach of stage tolerance.
whyNot.1: The approach holds the risk procedure, not individual risks.
whyNot.2: Responses are planned through the risk procedure run by the project manager; the team manager does not go to individual directors.

B.q: Tarnside College's governors have told the principal that the college cannot afford to spend more than 3% above the approved budget. During initiation, the deputy principal suggests the project board should decide how much financial risk the college as a whole is willing to take. Who should determine that risk appetite?
options: The project board, led by the executive
The project manager, Leah Whitfield
The governors, as the business layer
Project assurance, on the board's behalf
B.why: Risk appetite is determined by the business and applied by the project board when it sets risk tolerance (9.2.1).

whyNot.0: The board applies the appetite by setting risk tolerance; it does not determine the business's appetite.
whyNot.1: The project manager manages risk within the tolerances set above them.
whyNot.3: Project assurance provides independent checks for the board; it does not set appetite.

C.q: During initiation of Brennan Mutual's Project Skyline, the draft risk management approach includes the threat that Stratoshift's Pune team may lose key engineers, and names Arjun Menon to monitor it. Is this an appropriate application of the risk practice, and why?
options: Yes, because key threats should be visible in the PID
Yes, because a named person must act on each risk
No, because supplier risks belong to the senior supplier
No, because specific risks belong in the risk register
C.why: The risk management approach describes how risk will be managed; it does not contain specific risks, which are recorded in the risk register with their owners (9.5).

whyNot.0: The PID holds the approach, but individual risks are recorded in the register within the project log.
whyNot.1: Owners and action owners are agreed for each risk, but that does not explain why a specific risk is in the approach.
whyNot.2: The senior supplier is interested in supplier-side risks, but the error here is recording a specific risk in the approach.

C.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in its concept and recipe stage. Project manager Nadia Osei adds this entry to the risk register: 'The chefs are already two weeks behind on the two pan-fried recipes.' Is this an appropriate entry, and why?
options: Yes, because it threatens the fixed launch week
Yes, because threats and opportunities both go in the register
No, because it has already happened, so it is an issue
No, because recipe delays belong in the quality register
C.why: A risk is an uncertain event; a delay that has already occurred is an event needing project management consideration, which is an issue (9.1, 10.1). It may point to a risk cause, but it is not itself a risk.

whyNot.0: The delay does threaten the launch, but that does not make a current fact a risk.
whyNot.1: Both threats and opportunities do go in the register, but this entry is not uncertain, so it is not a risk.
whyNot.3: The quality register records quality activities and their results, not schedule delays.

C.q: Carrowford City Council's half marathon project is in its planning and approvals stage. Project manager Kezia Oduya registers: 'Because a national running magazine is covering city races this year, it may feature Carrowford, which would raise entries by about 1,000.' A colleague says opportunities do not belong in the risk register. Is the colleague right, and why?
options: Yes, because opportunities are recorded as business opportunities
Yes, because opportunities are handled by the business layer
No, because the register records threats and opportunities
No, because the entry is written as cause, event and effect
C.why: PRINCE2 uses 'threat' and 'opportunity' for negative and positive uncertain events, and both are recorded and managed in the risk register (9.1, 9.5).

whyNot.0: A business opportunity is a type of issue (something that has arisen), not an uncertain event; this is a risk.
whyNot.1: The business layer sets appetite; opportunities affecting project objectives are managed in the project.
whyNot.3: The entry is well written as cause, event and effect, but that does not explain why an opportunity may be in the register.

reteach.title: The rulebook and the logbook
reteach.question: A sailing club has a safety handbook and a hazard log. Which one is like the risk management approach, and which like the risk register?

blocks.body: The safety handbook says how hazards are spotted, rated and reported, and who does what: that is the risk management approach. The hazard log lists actual hazards, such as 'the slipway may be icy on winter mornings, so a member could fall', with when it is likely, how bad it would be, what will be done, who is in charge of it and who is gritting the slipway. That is the risk register, and each part matches a heading.

blocks.h: The hazard log as register headings
head: Log entry
Register heading
rows: Icy slipway; a member could fall
A broken wrist; boats out of use

blocks.text: If the slipway accident has already happened, it is an issue, not a risk. And the handbook never lists the icy slipway itself.

explain.body: Anything about how the project will identify, assess, respond to and report risks, or who does what in that procedure, goes in the risk management approach in the PID.

test.q: During initiation of Project Skyline, Mairi Campbell wants to record that each migration wave's risks will be reviewed weekly by the project manager and the Stratoshift delivery lead, using agreed five-point scales. Where should this be recorded?
options: In the risk register, under risk response
In the daily log, as a planned action
In the risk management approach
In the work package description for wave 1
test.why: A review procedure, its timing, scales and responsibilities describe how risk will be managed, so they belong in the risk management approach (9.5).

whyNot.0: A risk response is recorded against one specific risk, not a general review procedure.
whyNot.1: The daily log is the PM's informal diary, not the place for the agreed risk procedure.
whyNot.3: A work package description covers one package of work, while this procedure applies to every wave.

explain.body: Timing is proximity. An estimate of the effect in days or money is impact. What will be done is the response. Cause, event and effect together is the description.

test.q: Tarnside College is in the detailed design stage. A register entry for the threat of an asbestos removal overrun reads: 'Estimated effect: structural works would start about four weeks late and cost roughly £40,000 more.' Under which heading should this be recorded?
options: Proximity
Risk response
Risk owner
Impact
test.why: Impact is an estimate of the risk's effect on objectives, in the units of those objectives such as weeks and pounds (9.2, 9.5).

whyNot.0: Proximity is when the risk might occur, not the size of its effect.
whyNot.1: The response is the action planned, such as an extra survey, not the estimated effect.
whyNot.2: The risk owner heading names a person, not an estimate.

explain.body: The risk owner takes responsibility for responding to the risk. The risk action owner carries out a specific agreed action within that response.

test.q: On Carrowford City Council's half marathon project, the board names the corporate risk and insurance manager, Martin Cole, as the person responsible for managing the response to the threat that event insurance costs rise sharply. Under which heading should his name be recorded?
options: Risk action owner
Risk owner
Risk response
Risk description
test.why: The risk owner is the person assigned to take responsibility for responding to a risk (9.2).

whyNot.0: A risk action owner carries out a specific agreed action, usually at the risk owner's request.
whyNot.2: The response heading records what will be done, not who is responsible for it.
whyNot.3: The description records cause, event and effect, not a person.

explain.body: The project manager sets up the risk register in initiation and runs the procedure. Project support, where it exists, maintains the register on the PM's behalf.

test.q: Calderbrook's Permits Online project has a project support officer from the council's project management office. After each weekly risk review, someone must update the status and history of each risk in the register. Which role should do this?
options: Project support
Project assurance
The senior user
The team manager
test.why: Registers in the project log are set up by the project manager and maintained by project support where it exists (9.5, 4.3.2).

whyNot.1: Project assurance checks on the board's behalf and is kept separate from project support's administrative work.
whyNot.2: The senior user represents users on the board and does not administer registers.
whyNot.3: Team managers identify risks in their work packages and notify the project manager; they do not maintain the register.
